Priya (oncall SRE): Heads-up: us-west1 GPU pools are reporting degraded capacity and queueing. Pods stuck in Pending with message 'Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'.
Marco (infra): Confirmed. Cloud provider shows multiple preemptions + a capacity zone flapping. Latency spike in inference queues.
Ava (gpu-ops): We're at ~65% of committed capacity after autoscaler thrash. Can we fail traffic to us-west2?
Priya (oncall SRE): Yes. Planning DNS failover to route inference traffic away from us-west1. Current DNS TTL is 300s. Concern: propagation delays.
Jin (dns-eng): Route53 weighted records in use for model-api.redwood.ai. Current weight: us-west1=100, us-west2=0. TTL 300.
Kelsey (network): If we switch weights, some clients with long resolver caches (corporate ISPs) will still hit us-west1 for a while. We should lower TTL first, wait, then flip weight.
Priya (oncall SRE): Agreed. Proposed steps: 1) Set TTL -> 30s on the record. 2) Wait 90s. 3) Shift weight to us-west2 incrementally (50/50) then 0/100. 4) Watch healthchecks + autoscaler. 5) Revert TTL to 300 after stable.
Marco (infra): We can push TTL change now. Route53 CLI: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://ttl-change.json`
Jin (dns-eng): I'll apply TTL=30 now. Note: internal service discovery (consul) ignoring DNS TTLs; make sure proxies respect it.
Ava (gpu-ops): GPU pool in us-west2 has capacity to absorb spike but we should enable burst instances; enabling reserved burst in 1min.
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-20240720-34 - us-west1 GPU degradation. Pager duty notified.
Kelsey (network): Also consider updating any hardcoded IPs for static edge caches. Some clients resolve and pin IPs for longer than TTL. Not many but saw 2% traffic from legacy partners.
Priya (oncall SRE): Good call. @Lewis/product we might see a small error rate during switch. Heads-up to support.
Marco (infra): TTL change done. Verified via `dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-api.redwood.ai` still returns old IPs for some resolvers, but Route53 reports new TTL.
Jin (dns-eng): Wait 90s -> 120s to account for aggressive caches. Then I'll start shifting weights to 50/50 via console.
Ava (gpu-ops): Burst pools enabled in us-west2. Autoscaler target increased.
Priya (oncall SRE): Starting weight shift to 50/50. Monitoring p50/p95 latency, error rate, queue depth.
Marco (infra): Observability: queue depth dropping on us-west2, latency stable. Error rate slight bump 0.3% -> 0.6% (likely in-flight sessions tied to us-west1 connections).
Kelsey (network): We see some clients still hitting us-west1 due to corporate resolver caching (AS3462). Expect full cutover within ~10 minutes.
Priya (oncall SRE): Moving to 0/100.
Jin (dns-eng): Weight set to us-west1=0, us-west2=100. Route propagation check: `dig +trace model-api.redwood.ai` shows majority resolving to us-west2 IPs.
Ava (gpu-ops): us-west2 handling traffic. GPU utilization moderate. No queueing.
Priya (oncall SRE): Leaving TTL=30 for now. We'll watch for 30m then restore.
Marco (infra): Action item: post-incident runbook update to include TTL pre-change checklist and partner notification step.
Jin (dns-eng): Also add note about internal proxies that ignore DNS TTLs and to restart proxies if pinned IPs observed.
Priya (oncall SRE): Thanks team. Closing incident when metrics stable for 30m and no flapping.
Kelsey (network): FYI: doc for DNS failover procedure updated in runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/dns-failover (added steps + dig commands).
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-20240720-34 status -> monitoring.
Priya (oncall SRE): Final note: TTL reduction is low-risk but remember it increases DNS query volume and billing. We'll set TTL back to 300 after stabilization.
